# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Morales_2023_type1Diabetes"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Morales_2023_type1Diabetes"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12973> (open access; the Monolix
  project and model files are in Supplementary Materials S2 and S3)

# Population

The model was fitted to 1265 individuals with two or more islet
autoantibodies, pooled from two natural-history studies: the TrialNet Pathway
to Prevention study (n = 1006; relatives of people with type 1 diabetes) and
the TEDDY birth cohort (n = 259; children with HLA-conferred risk). Time zero
is a *derived baseline*: the earliest visit at which a participant had at
least two autoantibodies and a complete set of covariates. Participants who
already met a diabetes criterion at that visit (2-h OGTT glucose
>= 200 mg/dL, fasting glucose >= 126 mg/dL or HbA1c >= 6.5%) were excluded,
and follow-up was truncated at 6 years. Mean (SD) age at the derived baseline
was 12.7 (9.7) years (range 1-56); 56.1% were male; 89.6% were GADA
positive, 61.9% IA-2A positive, 52.6% IAA positive and 70.9% ZnT8A positive;
mean (SD) HbA1c was 5.1 (0.3)%, fasting glucose 88.8 (9.2) mg/dL and the
2-h / fasting glucose ratio 1.3 (0.4) (Morales 2023 Table 1). The 8341
2-h OGTT glucose (GLU120) observations and the time to clinical diagnosis
were fitted jointly in Monolix 2021R1 on a random 80% training split
(n = 1016).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Morales_2023_type1Diabetes")()$population`.

# Model structure

The longitudinal 2-h OGTT glucose follows a sigmoid Emax function of time
since the derived baseline (Eq. 1):

$$\mathrm{GLU120}_i(t) = DP_{0,i} + \frac{DP_{\max,i}\, t^{\gamma_i}}{DP_{50,i}^{\gamma_i} + t^{\gamma_i}}$$

and the time to diagnosis follows a Weibull hazard whose scale is shortened
by the individual predicted GLU120 (Eqs. 2 and 4):

$$T_e' = \exp\left(\ln T_e - \beta_{T_e} \ln\frac{\mathrm{GLU120}_i(t)}{112}\right),\qquad
h(t) = \frac{p}{T_e'}\left(\frac{t}{T_e'}\right)^{p-1}$$

In the model file the Weibull rate `lam = 1 / Te'` is carried as
`exp(llam_haz) * (glucose_2h / 112)^e_glucose_2h_haz`, which is the same
expression. The hazard integrates into the `cumhaz` state, and
`sur = exp(-cumhaz)` is the probability of remaining free of type 1 diabetes.
Covariates enter as power functions of the centred continuous covariate, or
as log-scale shifts for 0/1 indicators (Supplementary Equations S1 and S2).

# Deterministic checks of the model equations

The typical subject (GADA negative, IA-2A negative, every continuous
covariate at its centring value) is solved without random effects, and the
packaged outputs are compared with the closed forms of Eqs. 1 and 4 and
with a numerical integral of the hazard.

```{r deterministic}
mod <- readModelDb("Morales_2023_type1Diabetes")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

ref_subject <- data.frame(
  GADA_POS = 0,
  IA2A_POS = 0,
  HBA1C = 5.10576,
  FPG = 88.0112,
  OGTT_GLU_RATIO_BL = 1.25818
)
tgrid <- seq(0, 6, by = 0.25)
ev_typ <- data.frame(id = 1, time = tgrid, evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz") |>
  cbind(ref_subject)
typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ))

glu_closed <- function(t) 107.31 + 208.72 * t^1.75 / (6.09^1.75 + t^1.75)
haz_closed <- function(t) {
  te_prime <- exp(log(91.81) - 6.13 * log(glu_closed(t) / 112))
  1.20 / te_prime * (t / te_prime)^(1.20 - 1)
}
sur_closed <- vapply(
  tgrid,
  function(tt) {
    if (tt == 0) {
      return(1)
    }
    exp(-stats::integrate(haz_closed, 0, tt, rel.tol = 1e-10)$value)
  },
  numeric(1)
)

det_check <- data.frame(
  time = tgrid,
  glucose_2h = typ$glucose_2h,
  glucose_closed = glu_closed(tgrid),
  hazard = typ$hazard,
  hazard_closed = haz_closed(tgrid),
  sur = typ$sur,
  sur_closed = sur_closed
)
knitr::kable(
  det_check[det_check$time %in% 0:6, ],
  digits = c(2, 3, 3, 5, 5, 4, 4),
  row.names = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  # Eq. 1 and Eq. 4 are algebraic in the model, so they match exactly.
  max(abs(det_check$glucose_2h - det_check$glucose_closed)) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(det_check$hazard - det_check$hazard_closed)) < 1e-10,
  # The cumulative hazard is an ODE state (LSODA, rtol 1e-6); an error in
  # the hazard form or in Te moves survival at 6 years by > 0.05.
  max(abs(det_check$sur - det_check$sur_closed)) < 1e-3
)
```

## Effect of GLU120 on the Weibull scale (Figure 3)

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates the smooth of Figure 3 of Morales 2023: the Weibull scale Te' as a function of the 2-h OGTT glucose (Eq. 4). The published figure scatters simulated values around this relation."}
fig3 <- data.frame(glucose_2h = seq(50, 500, by = 2)) |>
  mutate(te_prime = 91.81 * (glucose_2h / 112)^(-6.13))
ggplot(fig3, aes(glucose_2h, te_prime)) +
  geom_line(colour = "tomato") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 400)) +
  labs(x = "GLU120 (mg/dL)", y = "Te' (years)") +
  theme_bw()
```

At 112 mg/dL Te' equals Te (91.8 years); at 150 mg/dL it falls to
`r signif(91.81 * (150 / 112)^-6.13, 3)` years and above 200 mg/dL it is
under 3 years, the steep fall shown by the smooth in Figure 3.

# Virtual cohort

Covariates are drawn independently from the Table 1 summaries of the full
analysis cohort: GADA and IA-2A positivity as Bernoulli draws (89.6% and
61.9%), HbA1c and fasting glucose as normal draws (5.1 (0.3)% and
88.8 (9.2) mg/dL) and the 2-h / fasting ratio as a normal draw (1.3 (0.4)).
Draws that the paper's inclusion rules would have excluded (HbA1c >= 6.5%,
fasting glucose >= 126 mg/dL, implied 2-h glucose >= 200 mg/dL) are
rejected, as are ratios below 0.5.

```{r cohort}
draw_cohort <- function(n) {
  out <- NULL
  while (is.null(out) || nrow(out) < n) {
    d <- data.frame(
      GADA_POS = stats::rbinom(4 * n, 1, 0.896),
      IA2A_POS = stats::rbinom(4 * n, 1, 0.619),
      HBA1C = stats::rnorm(4 * n, 5.1, 0.3),
      FPG = stats::rnorm(4 * n, 88.8, 9.2),
      OGTT_GLU_RATIO_BL = stats::rnorm(4 * n, 1.3, 0.4)
    )
    keep <- d$HBA1C < 6.5 &
      d$FPG < 126 &
      d$OGTT_GLU_RATIO_BL > 0.5 &
      d$FPG * d$OGTT_GLU_RATIO_BL < 200
    out <- rbind(out, d[keep, ])
  }
  out <- out[seq_len(n), ]
  out$id <- seq_len(n)
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

set.seed(20230503)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- draw_cohort(n_sub)
summary(cohort[, c("HBA1C", "FPG", "OGTT_GLU_RATIO_BL")])
colMeans(cohort[, c("GADA_POS", "IA2A_POS")])
```

# Visual predictive check (Figure 4)

Each subject is solved on a fine grid to 6 years. A diagnosis time is
drawn from the individual survival curve (the first time `sur` falls below
a uniform draw), and 2-h glucose observations, with residual error, are kept
only at half-yearly visits before diagnosis, because no OGTT is collected
after a diagnosis. Survival is summarised as the cohort mean of the
individual survival curves.

```{r vpc-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230503)
ev_vpc <- merge(cohort, data.frame(time = seq(0, 6, by = 0.05))) |>
  arrange(id, time) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz")
sim_vpc <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_vpc))

u_draw <- data.frame(id = cohort$id, u = stats::runif(n_sub))
event_time <- sim_vpc |>
  left_join(u_draw, by = "id") |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    t_event = if (any(sur < u)) min(time[sur < u]) else Inf,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

visits <- seq(0, 6, by = 0.5)
obs_vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  left_join(event_time, by = "id") |>
  filter(abs(time - round(time * 2) / 2) < 1e-8, time < t_event)

vpc_tab <- obs_vpc |>
  mutate(time = round(time * 2) / 2) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    p05 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = stats::median(sim),
    p95 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(vpc_tab, digits = 1)
```

```{r fig4a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4a of Morales 2023: simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the 2-h OGTT glucose among subjects not yet diagnosed. The published simulated percentiles lie near 72, 117 and 187 mg/dL throughout the 6 years."}
vpc_tab |>
  pivot_longer(c(p05, p50, p95), names_to = "percentile", values_to = "glucose") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, glucose, colour = percentile)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(72, 117, 187), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(p05 = "steelblue", p50 = "red", p95 = "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time from derived baseline (years)",
    y = "GLU120 (mg/dL)",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig4b}
surv_sim <- sim_vpc |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(sur = mean(sur), .groups = "drop")

# Figure 4b (training data), digitised by the maintainers: the dashed
# predicted median and the observed Kaplan-Meier curve.
fig4b_pred <- data.frame(time = c(2, 4, 6), published = c(0.82, 0.64, 0.53))
fig4b_obs <- data.frame(
  time = 1:6,
  observed_km = c(0.93, 0.83, 0.73, 0.67, 0.58, 0.51)
)

surv_cmp <- fig4b_pred |>
  left_join(
    surv_sim |> mutate(time = round(time, 2)),
    by = "time"
  ) |>
  mutate(difference = sur - published)
surv_cmp |>
  rename(
    "Time (years)" = time,
    "Published predicted median" = published,
    "Simulated mean survival" = sur,
    "Difference" = difference
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r fig4b-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4b of Morales 2023: proportion free of type 1 diabetes. Line: simulated cohort mean survival; points: digitised published predicted median (triangles) and observed Kaplan-Meier curve (circles)."}
ggplot(surv_sim, aes(time, sur)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = fig4b_obs,
    aes(time, observed_km),
    shape = 1,
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = fig4b_pred,
    aes(time, published),
    shape = 2,
    size = 2,
    colour = "steelblue"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time from derived baseline (years)",
    y = "Proportion free of type 1 diabetes"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig4-gate}
stopifnot(
  # Survival: the largest difference from the published median was
  # 0.02-0.064 over five seeds at 1, 2, 4 and 8 solver threads. Doubling
  # Te or halving beta_Te moves S(6) by more than 0.15.
  nrow(surv_cmp) == 3,
  max(abs(surv_cmp$difference)) < 0.10,
  # Glucose percentiles among undiagnosed subjects (Figure 4a). Over the
  # same runs the medians across visits of the 5th, 50th and 95th
  # percentiles were 62-73, 119-132 and 191-213 mg/dL.
  nrow(vpc_tab) == length(visits),
  dplyr::between(stats::median(vpc_tab$p50), 100, 150),
  dplyr::between(stats::median(vpc_tab$p05), 50, 90),
  dplyr::between(stats::median(vpc_tab$p95), 165, 245)
)
```

# Survival by baseline covariate (Figure 5)

Figure 5 of Morales 2023 shows the predicted survival of virtual cohorts in
which only one baseline characteristic differs. The paper does not describe
the other covariates of those cohorts; here each scenario takes the virtual
cohort above and sets the one covariate for every subject. Each scenario is
solved with the same seed, so the subjects carry the same random effects in
every scenario and the differences between scenarios come from the covariate
alone.

```{r fig5-sim}
scenarios <- list(
  list(panel = "GADA", var = "GADA_POS", value = 0, label = "Absent"),
  list(panel = "GADA", var = "GADA_POS", value = 1, label = "Present"),
  list(panel = "IA-2A", var = "IA2A_POS", value = 0, label = "Absent"),
  list(panel = "IA-2A", var = "IA2A_POS", value = 1, label = "Present"),
  list(panel = "HbA1c", var = "HBA1C", value = 4, label = "4"),
  list(panel = "HbA1c", var = "HBA1C", value = 4.5, label = "4.5"),
  list(panel = "HbA1c", var = "HBA1C", value = 5.5, label = "5.5"),
  list(panel = "HbA1c", var = "HBA1C", value = 6.5, label = "6.5")
)
fig5_grid <- seq(0, 6, by = 0.1)

run_scenario <- function(sc) {
  dat <- cohort
  dat[[sc$var]] <- sc$value
  ev <- merge(dat, data.frame(time = fig5_grid)) |>
    arrange(id, time) |>
    mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz")
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230503)
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev)) |>
    group_by(time) |>
    summarise(sur = mean(sur), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(panel = sc$panel, level = sc$label)
}
fig5_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(scenarios, run_scenario))

# The GADA panel again, with IA-2A negative and the continuous covariates
# at their centring values instead of drawn from the cohort.
cohort_ref <- cohort |>
  mutate(
    IA2A_POS = 0,
    HBA1C = 5.10576,
    FPG = 88.0112,
    OGTT_GLU_RATIO_BL = 1.25818
  )
gada_ref <- vapply(
  0:1,
  function(g) {
    ev <- merge(mutate(cohort_ref, GADA_POS = g), data.frame(time = c(0, 6))) |>
      arrange(id, time) |>
      mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz")
    rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230503)
    s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev))
    mean(s$sur[s$time == 6])
  },
  numeric(1)
)
```

```{r fig5-plot, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Morales 2023: simulated proportion free of type 1 diabetes by GADA status, IA-2A status and HbA1c at the derived baseline. Crosses mark the digitised 6-year values of the published curves."}
# Six-year values of the Figure 5 curves, digitised by the maintainers.
fig5_pub <- data.frame(
  panel = c("GADA", "GADA", "IA-2A", "IA-2A", "HbA1c", "HbA1c", "HbA1c", "HbA1c"),
  level = c("Absent", "Present", "Absent", "Present", "4", "4.5", "5.5", "6.5"),
  published = c(0.55, 0.73, 0.57, 0.45, 0.82, 0.68, 0.36, 0.18)
)
ggplot(fig5_sim, aes(time, sur, colour = level)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = fig5_pub,
    aes(x = 6, y = published, colour = level),
    shape = 4,
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time from derived baseline (years)",
    y = "Proportion free of type 1 diabetes",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig5-table}
fig5_cmp <- fig5_sim |>
  filter(abs(time - 6) < 1e-8) |>
  select(panel, level, simulated = sur) |>
  left_join(fig5_pub, by = c("panel", "level")) |>
  mutate(
    difference = simulated - published,
    deviation = panel == "GADA"
  )
stopifnot(nrow(fig5_cmp) == nrow(fig5_pub))

fig5_cmp |>
  rename(
    "Covariate" = panel,
    "Level" = level,
    "Simulated S(6 y)" = simulated,
    "Published S(6 y)" = published,
    "Difference" = difference,
    "Documented deviation" = deviation
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

s6 <- function(p, l) fig5_cmp$simulated[fig5_cmp$panel == p & fig5_cmp$level == l]
gated <- fig5_cmp[!fig5_cmp$deviation, ]
stopifnot(
  # Directions: with common random effects each covariate shifts every
  # subject's glucose curve, and so every survival curve, the same way.
  s6("GADA", "Present") > s6("GADA", "Absent"),
  s6("IA-2A", "Present") < s6("IA-2A", "Absent"),
  s6("HbA1c", "4") > s6("HbA1c", "4.5"),
  s6("HbA1c", "4.5") > s6("HbA1c", "5.5"),
  s6("HbA1c", "5.5") > s6("HbA1c", "6.5"),
  # Magnitudes for the IA-2A and HbA1c panels. Over five seeds at 1-8
  # solver threads the absolute differences were at most 0.085 and their
  # median at most 0.05.
  nrow(gated) == 6,
  stats::median(abs(gated$difference)) < 0.10,
  max(abs(gated$difference)) < 0.18,
  # GADA panel with reference covariates: still ordered by GADA status.
  gada_ref[2] > gada_ref[1]
)
```

The IA-2A and HbA1c panels are reproduced at six years to within
`r round(max(abs(gated$difference)), 2)` (see the table). The GADA panel is
reproduced in direction but not in level: with the other covariates drawn
from the Table 1 cohort, six-year survival is
`r round(s6("GADA", "Absent"), 2)` (absent) and
`r round(s6("GADA", "Present"), 2)` (present), compared with 0.55 and 0.73 in
Figure 5a. Holding IA-2A negative and the continuous covariates at their
centring values gives `r round(gada_ref[1], 2)` and
`r round(gada_ref[2], 2)`, closer to the figure, which suggests that the
Figure 5a cohort had a lower-risk covariate mix than the full analysis
cohort. The paper does not describe that cohort, so the panel is listed as a
deviation and gated on direction only.

# Why there is no NCA

The model has no drug input: it describes the natural history of
dysglycemia and progression to clinical type 1 diabetes, so there is no
exposure for PKNCA to summarise. Validation uses the deterministic checks of
the model equations above and comparison with the published visual
predictive check and covariate-scenario figures.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Parameter values: Table 2, with the correlations from the supplement.**
  The main-text Table 2 ('Final parameter estimates of the joint model') and
  the `<PARAMETER>` block of the Supplementary S2 Monolix project disagree on
  every value, and only S2 contains the inter-individual correlations. The
  model carries the Table 2 fixed effects, SDs and residual error, and the
  three correlations from S2 (the Table 2 SDs with the S2 correlations give
  a positive-definite matrix). Both sets give nearly the same typical
  GLU120 curve. The S2 values, for reference:

  | Parameter | Table 2 (used) | Supplementary S2 |
  |---|---|---|
  | DP50 (year) | 6.09 | 7.661 |
  | DPmax (mg/dL) | 208.72 | 285.44 |
  | gamma | 1.75 | 2.228 |
  | DP0 (mg/dL) | 107.31 | 107.85 |
  | Te (year) | 91.81 | 85.09 |
  | p | 1.20 | 1.225 |
  | beta_Te | 6.13 | 6.028 |
  | GADA on DPmax | -0.73 | -0.676 |
  | HbA1c on DPmax | 8.92 | 8.859 |
  | IA-2A on DP50 | -0.71 | -0.724 |
  | GLU0 on DP0 | 0.88 | 0.866 |
  | GLU ratio on DP0 | 0.79 | 0.785 |
  | SD DP50 / DPmax / gamma / DP0 | 0.72 / 1.69 / 1.76 / 0.043 | 0.857 / 1.428 / 1.531 / 0.0476 |
  | Proportional residual | 0.16 | 0.1643 |
  | r(DP0, DPmax) / r(gamma, DPmax) / r(gamma, DP0) | not reported | 0.849 / 0.728 / 0.371 |

* **Covariate centring values** are the weighted means printed in the S2
  `[COVARIATE]` block (HbA1c 5.10576%, GLU0 88.0112 mg/dL, ratio 1.25818),
  not the Table 1 means; these are the values the final model used.
* **Branched sigmoid.** The sigmoid fraction is evaluated in the two
  branches of Supplementary S3 (`(t/DP50)^gamma` below DP50,
  `(DP50/t)^gamma` above it). The result is identical to Eq. 1, but it
  avoids `Inf / Inf` for the large individual gamma values that an SD of
  1.76 on the log scale produces.
* **Hazard at time zero.** Supplementary S3 sets the hazard to 0 for
  t < 0.001 year. With p = 1.20 the Weibull hazard is already 0 at t = 0
  and negligible over that interval, so the guard is not reproduced.
* **TTE output.** The model provides the cumulative hazard and survival
  probability as outputs for simulation; no time-to-event likelihood is
  attached, so a refit of the event data would add one.
* **Virtual cohort.** The covariates are drawn independently from the
  Table 1 summaries; the correlations between them (for example between
  fasting glucose and the 2-h / fasting ratio) are not reported. The
  simulated survival nonetheless follows the published prediction closely.
* **Figure values** were digitised by the maintainers from Figures 4b and 5
  and are accurate to about 0.02.
* **Covariates screened but not retained** (age, BMI, sex, autoantibody
  counts and combinations, C-peptide measures, HLA risk, first-degree
  relative) are not in the model; age, BMI and sex are recorded in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
